headline: Trump bans major media outlets from White House press briefings

sources.excerpt: President Donald Trump said he is banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, effective immediately, “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” In a Truth Social post Friday, he baselessly accused the three credible news outlets of reporting falsely on him and his administration, but he did not point to specific coverage examples. He also said bans on more outlets will follow, teeing up further escalation in his ongoing war against press freedom. At a press conference late Friday afternoon, Trump accused the outlets of being “one-sided” and said, “They purposely write negative news. And they do that because they want to try and diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration.” “It’s really just accumulative stories over the last few years. You get sick of it,” he said in response to a reporter’s question on the timing of his announcement. Later, asked what the ban would mean in practice, Trump needed clarification on “which ban,” suggesting he had enacted too many to keep tabs on. “Oh, the ban on the free press, right?” he said. “Very simple ban: I don’t want them in my office. I don’t want them here. I would say the ban would go as far as you can.” The president insisted during the press conference that the U.S. is thriving, refusing to contend with polls suggesting everyday Americans are seriously struggling economically, particularly since he chose to start a war with Iran. At another point, Trump responded with sarcasm when a reporter began a question by stating that freedom of the press is enshrined in the First Amendment, saying, “Oh, thank you for telling me.” When the reporter asked Trump whether he was trying to “intimidate” the press, he replied with a personal insult: “No. I dislike dishonest press, like you. I think you’re terrible.” CNN reported Friday that its journalists remained at the White House and that there was “no indication” Trump had taken any steps to put the supposed ban in place. The network said in a statement that it stands behind its “fair and accurate” reporting. “We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do that reporting without hindrance or interference from the government,” CNN said, adding that the ban would be an illegal assault on press freedom if enacted. Politico similarly defended itself. “Politico will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones,” the outlet said in a statement. “We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them.” MS NOW declined HuffPost’s request for comment. Jacqui Heinrich, Fox News’ senior white house correspondent and president of the White House Correspondents’ Association, condemned the president’s decision in a statement, saying that press freedom “does not depend on whether the president likes a news organization’s coverage, agrees with its reporting, or approves of the questions its journalists ask.” “This is about more than the rights of journalists,” she continued. “It is about the right of the American people to receive a full and independent account of the activities, policies and decisions of whoever occupies the nation’s highest office.” Trump did not say which other outlets he might try to ban from the White House next when a reporter asked, but in his reply, he disparaged both The New York Times and The Washington Post. The move represents Trump’s latest attack on the free press, which is often likened to the fourth pillar of democracy because it holds the government accountable and keeps the public informed. Earlier this year, the Pentagon banned journalists who did not comply with new, unprecedented rules. The White House also previously attempted to ban The Associated Press from accessing the People’s House for coverage. However, a judge ruled that blocking select journalists over their reporting violated the First Amendment. Late last year, the Trump administration launched a “media offender” website to counter reports and name an offender of the week. The site lists many major news organizations, including ABC News, Fox News and The Washington Post. And the Federal Communications Commission, run by Trump crony Brendan Carr, has gone after several news organizations, including ABC, CBS and NBC. The latest attack was met with swift criticism by press freedom defenders. Bruce D. Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said a ban of this nature would be unconstitutional. “The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can’t ban others because it doesn’t like their reporting,” Brown said in a statement. “This is textbook viewpoint discrimination and will be quickly struck down by the courts if challenged.” National Press Club President Mark Schoeff Jr. said that “Banning news organizations from the White House based on the administration’s disapproval of their coverage is a clear attempt to control which voices are allowed to witness and report on the exercise of presidential power.”

President Donald Trump on Friday said he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters from the White House. Trump said on social media the ban was "effective immediately" as a result of what he called "their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS." "Media Outlets shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America," the president wrote on Truth Social. "Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow." Trump's move escalates his ongoing battle with news organizations whose coverage he dislikes. Last year, the administration banned the Associated Press from several events because it continued to use Gulf of Mexico instead of the president's new name for the body of water. In 2018, CNN reporter Jim Acosta lost his credential to the White House until a federal judge ordered the pass restored. Seth Stern, advocacy chief at Freedom of the Press Foundation, said "it's difficult to imagine a more blatant violation of the First Amendment. It's also hard to imagine a dumber move," Stern added in a statement. "The historically unpopular president has been retaliating against the press for years, but it hasn't helped him. The press keeps exposing his corruption and his failures. These outrageous attacks only demonstrate how scared he is of an informed public." It is unclear when the ban will go into effect. CNN said its reporters were still stationed in their White House workspace Friday evening. "CNN stands fully behind our White House team and their fair and accurate reporting," the network said in a statement. "We have a right under the U.S. Constitution to do that reporting without hindrance or interference from the government. Should the ban which President Trump threatened go ahead, it would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right." Politico said it would "continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones." "We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them," the news outlet said in a statement. Speaking to reporters Friday night, Trump threatened to take his ban even further. "There may be others to join them," he said, singling out The New York Times and The Washington Post.

Trump bans CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House ‘effective immediately’ in latest blast at media. By Steven Nelson. Published Sep. 18, 2026. Updated Sep. 18, 2026, 5:34 p.m. ET. WASHINGTON — President Trump claimed in an unprecedented announcement Friday that he was banning CNN, MS Now and Politico journalists from the White House “effective immediately” for allegedly reporting “Fake News.” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that he wanted the ban to “go as far as you can,” though the practical effect was not immediately clear. Reporters from all three outlets remained on the White House grounds as of Friday evening. Any ban, if imposed, would trigger First Amendment litigation. It was unclear whether Trump intends for the outlets to be booted from the “pool” rotations of reporters given special access to the president or banished altogether from the White House grounds — though the president indicated he favored the latter. “The ban on the free press, right? A very simple ban,” Trump explained. “I don’t want them in my office. I don’t want them here. I would say the ban would go as far as you can, and if they could straighten themselves out, I’d love it.” Trump added that his announcement targeting the three outlets was result of “cumulative stories over the last two years” rather than any single report, adding: “You get sick of it.” “The ban is because they are fake news, they cannot write the truth … Now, if they want to write such content, that’s fine. But I don’t have to let them into my — into the people’s house.” In a statement, CNN insisted the network has a constitutional right to report “without hindrance or interference from the government.” “Should the ban which President Trump threatened go ahead, it would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right,” the network said. White House Correspondents’ Association president Jacqui Heinrich said: “The Constitution protects the freedom of the press from government interference. That protection does not depend on whether the president likes a news organization’s coverage, agrees with its reporting, or approves of the questions its journalists ask.” “This is about more than the rights of journalists. It is about the right of the American people to receive a full and independent account of the activities, policies and decisions of whoever occupies the nation’s highest office,” said Heinrich, a Fox News correspondent. “The WHCA stands in defense of our colleagues at CNN, MSNOW, and Politico who are being singled out for doing their jobs.” Trump himself admitted his proposed restrictions might not hold up in court, saying, “It depends on the judge you get, to be honest with you.” The White House last year removed the Associated Press, which previously attended all presidential events, from pooled access after the wire service refused to go along with his rebrand of the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America.” The AP sued and was later allowed into the daily print pool rotation, made up of more than 30 outlets. That legal fight is ongoing. Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders, a former White House press secretary from Trump’s first term, defended the president as she attended an unrelated healthcare announcement. “I think the president is right to support the First Amendment, but he’s also right to ask that you be honest and fair,” she said. The prospective order has major practical implications — potentially upending the long-standing ability of reporters to gain access to the White House, even if events that require an RSVP oftentimes feature opaque access hurdles. CNN is a member of the TV pool rotation that ensures presidential remarks are broadcast live from the White House. The “five families” that operate that feed — whose number include ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox News — are particularly powerful in negotiating press access with Trump, who often demands network coverage of his comments. Reporters from each of the three outlets also serve in pool rotations that — until now — have been largely respected by the second Trump administration. CNN has a six-person booth at the White House and its reporters file stand-ups from tents on the North Lawn, as does MS Now. Politico, like other print publications, has an assigned workspace adjacent to the White House briefing room. Trump threatened in his Truth Social announcement that “Other Fake News Media Outlets” would henceforth be banned and specifically called out the Washington Post and New York Times in the Oval Office. “We’re probably not going to display the paper anymore in the White House, those papers, but we haven’t taken the step of throwing them out. But they’re fake news, totally,” he said. “New York Times is so fake. Washington Post is disgusting. I mean, they’re disgusting. I don’t get it.”
